date_label: Before Smith went to Ross in early 1903 - start not established.
summary: Frederick 'Freddie' Smith lived with George Ives before he left him for Robert Ross. Brian Lewis states that Smith left Ives for Ross, and quotes Ives's diary to that effect (Ives asserting that he was "not jealous"). Cook likewise records Smith among the household's long-term residents before he moved in with Ross. Fryer dates Ross's meeting with Smith to early 1903, which puts the end of the Ives connection at or before that.
certainty_reasoning: The attestation currently available is Brian Lewis's: Lewis quoted the diary passage aloud and the recording has not yet been transcribed, so no participant wording is held here. Once the diary page has been requested from HRC and verified on the page, this edge can become self-reported.

order_hint.why: Undated pending transcription; placed just before Ross's meeting with Smith in early 1903, which is the latest the Ives attachment can have run.

sources.supports: That Smith was attached to Ives before Ross, and left Ives for him. Brian Lewis quoted a diary passage supporting this.
sources.provenance: Unpublished video call; a recording exists but has not yet been transcribed. Entered now so the connection is on the map, marked pending until the diary passage can be quoted and cited by volume and date.

sources.quote: Also in the house were Pug and Elephant and other intimate male friends of Ives who became housemates for often extended periods before moving on - often to marry, or in the case of Freddie Smith to move in with Robbie Ross who was a good friend of both Ives and Wilde.
sources.context: Cook, on the turnover of the Adelaide Road household
sources.supports: Freddie Smith's household membership and his departure to live with Robert Ross - the Ives-circle/Wilde-circle bridge.
